candidates.title: Locked Keepsake Box
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered a small keepsake box stayed locked when its owner needed an old photograph before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they tried a spare key, but it did not fit the delicate latch; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a stamped mark beneath the box named the original village craftsman; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they asked the craftsman to unlock it without damage and returned the photograph, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Windmill That Stopped
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the community windmill stopped turning while the grain mill waited for flour before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they oiled the axle, but the sails still shuddered without completing a turn; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a bird's abandoned nesting twine had wound tightly around the brake lever; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they unwound the twine, checked the brake, and restarted the mill for the bakers, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Sign That Pointed Backward
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered a freshly painted direction sign sent festival visitors toward a closed road before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they turned the sign around, but visitors arriving from the other side became confused; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized the painter had copied the arrows from a reflection in a shop window; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they repainted the arrows from a verified map and guided everyone to the fair, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
